A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IAG. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original grounding-attack experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, defense evaluations, timing measurements and real-world examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original grounding experiments and adds baseline comparisons, perceptual measurements, defense tests and VQA experiments, including results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The text-conditioned U-Net, additive triggers, poisoning pipeline and joint language-model training remain. v3 Section 3.3 replaces v2's smoothed pixel-only reconstruction loss with weighted L1 and LPIPS terms, using weights 1 and 0.05. Appendix N adapts the same mechanism to sentence targets for VQA. Newly specified U-Net layer sizes establish additional documentation, not an architectural change.

E1.justification: v3 adds Flickr30k Entities and systematic ShowUI-Web evaluation, attacker-targeted VQA on OKVQA and VQA-v2 using Hate-Speech-18 sentences, and benign-task evaluation on RealWorldQA and MMBench. These substantially broaden the evaluated data and tasks. COCO-2017 remains in Table 8; real-world GUI examples were already present in v2.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 introduces evaluated One-to-N, Random, Imperio and Marksman comparisons across the victim models. The static-attack comparison changes from BadEncoder and TrojVLM in v2 Table 2 to BadVLMDriver, TrojVLM and VLOOD in v3 Table 10. BadEncoder is removed, while TrojVLM is retained under a revised protocol.

E3.justification: The static-baseline evaluation changes from v2's restricted 100-target setting to v3's per-target triggers with Sentence-BERT semantic matching at inference. Added experiments introduce ShowUI center-point correctness, L1/LPIPS/PSNR measurements, and a 1,000-target-sentence VQA poisoning protocol. Table 6 changes from original-dataset expression statistics to attack-image counts; this alone does not establish that retained RefCOCO splits were changed.

E4.justification: v3 adds quantitative reconstruction-loss ablations, a beta sweep measuring attack success versus image quality, and defenses using mean/median filtering, JPEG compression, clean retraining and INT8 quantization. It also adds attention-map analysis and expands the webpage case study to multiple targets within one image. These investigate perceptual tradeoffs, practical robustness and attack mechanisms beyond v2's analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions describe timing measurements over 10 sampled questions and report means and standard deviations. Neither reports attack-training seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. v3's probabilistic theorem is theoretical analysis, not new empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous baseline, defense, perceptual and VQA results are added. Retained rows also change: InternVL RefCOCO-val ASR is 65.9% in v2 versus 66.9% in v3, and LLaVA RefCOCOg-val ASR/BA changes from 41.3/77.3 to 47.3/77.6. The no-language-loss ablation's benign accuracies change from zero to 90.2/85.3/86.6. v3 also reports Imperio outperforming IAG on InternVL/RefCOCOg, 52.4% versus 50.2%. These are reported revisions and additions, not established same-setting gains across versions.

T1.justification: v2 Section 5 and Appendix A's existence and convergence propositions, including universal-approximation and Polyak-Lojasiewicz arguments, are removed. v3 Section 3.6 and Appendix B replace them with log-likelihood margins, perceptual-subspace and local-linearization assumptions, a probabilistic margin lower bound, and identifiability/perceptual-tradeoff corollaries.

C1.justification: The central arbitrary-target grounding attack claim remains. However, v3 removes existence/convergence guarantees and a new attack dataset from the headline contributions, emphasizing superiority over input-aware competitors and broader transferability instead. Its abstract newly claims transferability across models, although the reported experiments do not clearly specify a source-to-target-model transfer test.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving text-conditioned feature alignment, limitations of competing generators, and attention shifting toward attack targets. It interprets JPEG defense through its attack-success/benign-accuracy tradeoff and discusses preservation of other benign tasks. The no-language-loss ablation is now interpreted as failed target alignment despite preserved benign grounding, unlike v2's all-zero results.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents generator channels and attention heads, baseline adaptations, attack-data examples, image-subset counts, semantic-matching implementation, and defense parameters. It specifies 50-token ShowUI targets and reports four RTX6000 GPUs instead of one; Table 7's core training hyperparameters remain unchanged. Conversely, v2 Appendix I's commitment to release code and datasets upon acceptance disappears.

R1.justification: v3 substantially repositions IAG against arbitrary-target and input-aware attacks, especially Imperio, Marksman and One-to-N, explaining alleged architectural limitations. It adds GUI-grounding and VisualTrap context, perceptual-metric literature, and references supporting the new tasks. Much of the approximation/convergence literature supporting v2's removed proofs is dropped.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, methodology and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Eight main sections become five, with threat modeling integrated into Backgrounds and theory incorporated into Methodology. The separate Discussion is dissolved, appendices are substantially reorganized, and the title and author information change.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redrawn, Figure 3 replaces some cases, and plots are restyled. Table 1 becomes a large baseline comparison while the fuller IAG results move to appendix Table 8. New architecture, perceptual, hyperparameter and VQA tables and an attention visualization substantially change the displays. Cross-dataset results and retained real-world illustrations are relocated within a reformatted supplement.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses two important weaknesses in v2: comparison only against static attacks in a restricted target setting, and largely qualitative evidence of imperceptibility. Relevant input-aware competitors, quantitative perceptual tests, practical defenses and benign-task checks provide much stronger validation, while architecture and baseline details improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removed release commitment and remaining inconsistencies, including Algorithm 1 omitting the stated LPIPS weight and the abstract asserting cross-model transfer without a clearly documented corresponding experiment.
